name: Kubernetes
description: Register Kubernetes clusters and give agents scoped, human-approved access to them through an mcp__cockpit-k8s__* server. The plugin talks to the cluster itself (via the official Kubernetes client) and keeps the credentials — an agent never gets a kubeconfig. Every call is gated: opening a cluster asks for consent, a namespace outside the cluster's allowed list asks each session (reads included), and every change asks afresh and is never remembered. Cluster-scoped resources, exec and port-forward are off until you turn them on per cluster. A port-forward tunnel shows in the status bar with an operator-only Kill and auto-closes. Helm releases can be read (helm_list/helm_status/helm_history/helm_values/helm_manifest) straight from their release secrets, no helm binary needed, and get_resource flags a resource as Helm-managed. helm_rollback rolls a release back to an earlier revision by applying the manifest that revision stored, and helm_upgrade upgrades a release by rendering the chart with a helm dry run and applying that; both put the literal manifest diff on the approval, are deliberately not full helm parity (no three-way merge, no hooks), and there is no install or uninstall. Configure clusters in the plugin settings: point at a kubeconfig file (e.g. ~/.kube/config, read live) and pick a context from it, or paste a kubeconfig which is stored under the secret layer.
author: Cockpit
